canonical_statement: For Borel probability measures mu and nu on the real line, if their characteristic functions agree at every real argument, then mu = nu.

canonical_formal_target.declaration_or_expression: forall (mu nu : Measure Real), IsProbabilityMeasure mu -> IsProbabilityMeasure nu -> (forall t : Real, integral (fun x : Real => Complex.exp (Complex.I * (t * x))) mu = integral (fun x : Real => Complex.exp (Complex.I * (t * x))) nu) -> mu = nu
canonical_formal_target.note: Provisional mathematical shape only; namespaces, coercions, integrability API, and minimal imports are deliberately not asserted as elaborated Lean.

domain_and_universes: mu nu : Borel measures on Real; Prop in Lean universe 0
quantifiers: t : Real in the pointwise characteristic-function hypothesis
hypotheses: mu and nu are probability measures
for every real t, the characteristic-function integrals of mu and nu are equal
conclusion: mu = nu as measures on the Borel sigma-algebra of Real

alternate_encodings.target: real-valued random variables X and Y with identical characteristic functions have identical distributions
alternate_encodings.relationship: pushforward-law specialization of the measure root

alternate_encodings.target: finite Borel measures with equal Fourier transforms are equal
alternate_encodings.relationship: a stronger Fourier-transform uniqueness theorem may imply the probability-measure root

excluded_substitutions: moment sequences uniquely determine a distribution
equality at a finite set of frequencies
degenerate_cases: Atomic and Dirac probability laws are included. No density, moment, compact-support, or nondegeneracy assumption may be added.
